subtopics.title: The Working Tool — Two Points and One Equality

questions.question: The conservation equality $E_{k1} + E_{p1} = E_{k2} + E_{p2}$ may be used only when:
options: The path is a straight line
No friction or air resistance acts
The two points are at the same height

questions.question: An object at the highest point of its vertical flight has, at that instant:
The best place for the reference level, where h = 0, is usually:
options: The lowest of the two points being compared
The highest point on the track

questions.question: Unlike the equations of motion, the energy method never needs:
options: The time taken or the shape of the path

subtopics.title: Straight Up and Straight Down — Throws and the Pendulum

questions.question: A ball is thrown up at 15 m/s. Ignoring air resistance, $\frac{1}{2}v^2 = 9,8h$ gives a maximum height of:
Ignoring air resistance, the ball's speed when it returns to the thrower's hand is:
options: Exactly 15 m/s — the journey is symmetric

questions.question: A pendulum bob is released 0,2 m above its lowest point. Its speed at the bottom is $\sqrt{2 \times 9,8 \times 0,2}$, which is:
Why can the bob never rise higher than 0,2 m on the far side of the swing?
options: That would need more mechanical energy than it was given at release
Gravity is stronger on the far side
Its mass increases as it swings

subtopics.title: The Roller Coaster — Working the Big One

questions.question: The 200 kg car crests the 25 m hill at 3 m/s. Its mechanical energy at the top is:
At the bottom, $100v^2 = 49\,900$ gives a speed of:
A learner ignores the car's 3 m/s at the crest. The specific error is:
options: Dropping the initial kinetic energy of 900 J from the total

questions.question: At 10 m height on the descent, $E_k = 49\,900 - 19\,600 = 30\,300$ J, so the speed there is:

subtopics.title: Inclined Planes and the Independence of Path

questions.question: A skateboarder starts from rest 5 m up a frictionless ramp. The speed at the bottom, $\sqrt{2 \times 9,8 \times 5}$, is:
A steep ramp and a long gentle ramp both drop 5 m. Ignoring friction, the finishing speeds:
options: Are higher on the steep ramp
Are equal — only the drop in height matters
Are higher on the long ramp
Depend on the length of each ramp

questions.question: In conservation-of-energy problems, the syllabus says the path taken can be ignored because the only relevant quantities are:
options: The track length and the slope angle
The object's speed and its height above the reference point

questions.question: The moment a question introduces friction, the equality $E_{k1} + E_{p1} = E_{k2} + E_{p2}$:
options: Becomes false — mechanical energy decreases as heat is generated
Holds if the mass is doubled
Holds only at the reference level

questions.question: On a swing, your speed is greatest:
options: At the bottom of the arc
At the top of the far side

questions.question: Released from rest, the far side of the swing lifts you:
options: To the same height as the release, never higher
To a height that depends on your mass

questions.question: A swing left alone dies down because:
options: Air resistance withdraws a little mechanical energy on every pass, leaving as heat
Gravity gets weaker with each pass
Its energy is destroyed at the bottom of each arc

questions.question: Two skaters drop 5 m from rest, one down a steep face and one down a lazy slope. At the bottom:
options: The steep-face skater is slower but arrives later
Both move at 9,90 m/s — the steep one just arrives sooner

questions.question: For the energy ledger, the only two things that matter about a position are:
options: How long the track is and how steep

questions.question: The coaster car crosses the crest at 3 m/s. Its 900 J of kinetic energy at the top:
options: Must be added to the 49 000 J of potential energy in the total
Can be ignored because it is small

subtopics.title: Why the Second Hill Is Always Lower

questions.question: Every hill after a roller coaster's first hill is lower because:
options: The car cannot buy more height than the energy banked at the first crest
The track gets cheaper to build lower down

questions.question: On a real track with friction, later hills must shrink by even more, because:
options: The account leaks — heat and noise take a toll on every metre of track
The car gets lighter during the ride

questions.question: Which words in a question are the 'seal' that permits using the conservation equality?
At Grade 10, when friction IS present, an energy question typically expects you to:
options: Calculate the exact heat with the work-energy theorem
State that mechanical energy decreased and that the loss became heat
